title: 2026-11-25_XOR.DDoS_Malware_Investigation_d1f
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised Linux-based host that has been infected with the XOR.DDoS malware. This malware is known to force infected hosts to participate in large DDoS attack campaigns. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activities on the compromised host, understand the malware's behavior, and gather evidence for further investigation.
outcomes: Identify suspicious services and their associated network ports.
Analyze systemd timers and services to understand persistence mechanisms.
Investigate lateral movement activities and unauthorized file transfers.

levels.title: Introduction

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH:
   ```bash
   ssh cyrano@target
   ```
2. List all services, including inactive ones:
   ```bash
   systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```
3. Look for unfamiliar or suspicious service names. Pay attention to services with unusual descriptions or those that are not part of standard system services.
4. Identify the suspicious service. In this case, the service name is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is related to network communication.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH:
   ```bash
   ssh cyrano@target
   ```
2. Check the status of the suspicious service identified in the previous task:
   ```bash
   systemctl status bkd.service
   ```
3. Examine the service configuration to find the port number:
   ```bash
   systemctl cat bkd.service
   ```
4. Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration. The port number is specified as an argument to the command.
5. The port number is `4444`.

levels.title: Identify Lateral Movement Service
levels.content: Investigate the compromised host to identify the component responsible for transferring files to another host. Unusual file synchronization activity has been detected between systems in the environment.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH:
   ```bash
   ssh cyrano@target
   ```
2. List all services, including inactive ones:
   ```bash
   systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```
3. Look for services related to file transfer or synchronization. Pay attention to services with unusual names or those that are not part of standard system services.
4. Identify the suspicious service. In this case, the service name is `payload-transfer.service`.
5. Check the status of the suspicious service:
   ```bash
   systemctl status payload-transfer.service
   ```
6. Examine the service configuration to understand its behavior:
   ```bash
   systemctl cat payload-transfer.service
   ```
7. The service is responsible for transferring files to `next-target`.
